reason: 1899 FA Cup Final: Sheffield United beat Derby County 4-1 at Crystal Palace, their first FA Cup (confirmed as their 4th by 1925, so 1899 was indeed first). Derby (Boag, 12') led at half-time; United scored four second-half goals (Bennett, Beer, Almond, Priest 89'). Hint accurate — Priest is 'among' not sole scorer. Distractors (Southampton, Notts County, Tottenham Hotspur) are all real, era-appropriate opponents of Sheffield United in other finals, correctly wrong here. No odd-one-out issue (Southampton is the format outlier but is a distractor, not the answer).

1902 FA Cup Final: Sheffield United 1-1 Southampton (Common/Wood), replay won 2-1 (Hedley, Barnes vs Brown). Southampton were indeed still a Southern League club. Both legs at Crystal Palace. Distractors Everton, Sunderland, Derby are real clubs of the era but not this final's opponent.

1915 FA Cup Final: Sheffield United 3-0 Chelsea at Old Trafford, known as the Khaki Cup Final for the many uniformed soldiers in the crowd; the Earl (Lord) of Derby presented the cup and urged enlistment, matching the hint exactly. Distractors are real nicknames of other finals (White Horse Final = 1923, Matthews Final = 1953) or a plausible-but-fictitious label (Munich Final), all correctly wrong for 1915.
1925 FA Cup Final: Sheffield United 1-0 Cardiff City at Wembley, Fred Tunstall scoring after 30 minutes; this remains United's last FA Cup win (still true as of 2026). Hint fully accurate.

26 Dec 1979 'Boxing Day Massacre': Sheffield Wednesday 4-0 Sheffield United at Hillsborough, attendance 49,309 (record for third-tier football). Ian Mellor opened the scoring with a 25-yard strike, followed by goals from Curran, Smith and King — hint detail confirmed via multiple sources including a Yorkshire Post obituary piece on Mellor.

Dave Bassett signed Brian Deane from Doncaster Rovers for £25,000 in summer 1988; Deane went on to partner Tony Agana and drove back-to-back promotions. Verified each distractor was NOT signed from Doncaster in 1988: Keith Edwards came from Hull City (March 1988), Bob Booker came from Brentford (late 1988), Carl Bradshaw was a Sheffield United academy product with no Doncaster link — all real Bassett-era Blades, correctly wrong.

1989-90 Second Division: Leeds United and Sheffield United both finished on 85 points; Leeds took the title on goal difference (+27 vs +20) and both were promoted. Barnsley, Huddersfield Town and Bradford City are genuine Yorkshire clubs (satisfying the stem's qualifier) but were not in contention that season, so they're correctly wrong distractors.

Harry Johnson is Sheffield United's all-time record goalscorer with 201 goals (1919-1930/1916-1931 spell). Confirmed all distractors are lower and correctly wrong: Alan Woodward 158 league goals (post-war record), Jimmy Hagan ~117-151 goals, Keith Edwards 171 goals across two spells. None approaches 201.
